fatal_errors: The predicted 10–20% lattice-parameter increase is unsupported and physically implausible as ordinary thermal expansion for this alloy.
The hypothesis misses the central observed mechanism: surface-energy-driven Au/Cu segregation, melting, and evaporation associated with active rather than sluggish diffusion.
The stated conditions incorrectly combine vacuum and atmospheric pressure and use heating rates and an upper temperature that do not match the target protocol.
The proposed measurements cannot detect the key composition-dependent surface segregation or distinguish kinetic instability from entropy stabilization.
explanation: In situ heating TEM is directionally appropriate for atomic-scale investigation, but the reconstruction omits aberration-corrected STEM-EDS and complementary molecular-dynamics simulations. It also gives incorrect conditions and even misstates the alloy composition as AuCoCoCuNiPt. The generic thermal-diffusion mechanism has only weak overlap with the target and replaces the relevant shape- and size-dependent Au/Cu surface segregation with lattice strain. Consequently, its predicted lattice expansion does not agree with the observed particle reshaping, loss of small particles, Au/Cu evaporation, and approximately 22% size reduction. Although the proposed temperature-dependent lattice measurement is falsifiable, it is poorly discriminating for the scientific question and has no supporting evidence.
